def clean_check_command(f):
    @wraps(f)
    def inner(ctx, *args, **kwargs):
        # TODO: Remove this soon, for now it keeps a legacy behavior
        kwargs.pop("key", None)
        kwargs.pop('proxy_protocol', None)
        kwargs.pop('proxy_host', None)
        kwargs.pop('proxy_port', None)

        apply_remediations = kwargs.get('apply_remediations', False)

        if apply_remediations:
            key = ctx.params.get('key', None) or (ctx.obj.auth.client.get_authentication_type() if ctx.obj and ctx.obj.auth and ctx.obj.auth.client else None)
            
            # Check if key is provided
            from safety.auth.utils import is_valid_credential
            try:
                authenticated = ctx.obj.auth.client.is_using_auth_credentials()
            except Exception:
                authenticated = False

            if not authenticated:
                click.secho(
                    "The --apply-security-updates option needs authentication. See https://docs.safetycli.com/safety-docs/support/invalid-api-key-error.",
                    file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(EXIT_CODE_VULNERABILITIES_FOUND + 1)

            files = kwargs.get('files', ())
            if not files:
                click.secho(
                    '--apply-security-updates only works with files; use the "-r" option to specify files to remediate.',
                    file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(EXIT_CODE_FAILURE)

        return f(ctx, *args, **kwargs)

    return inner
